findings.title: Post-rename fsync failure publishes output but falsely claims retained pending evidence
findings.proof: os.replace consumes pending at line 450, then fsync_dir(output.parent) can fail. The exception handler writes PUBLICATION-FAILED.json only if pending.exists(). An injected failure on that final parent fsync deterministically produced ProjectionError, OUTPUT_EXISTS=True, PENDING_COUNT=0 and FAILURE_MARKER_IN_OUTPUT=False, while the message claimed intermediate evidence was retained at the vanished pending path.
findings.impact: The caller receives failure while an unclassified, durability-unknown output exists at the final path. This violates atomic failure classification and can be mistaken for a valid generated bundle.
findings.minimumRepair: Track whether rename committed. Before rename, retain and classify pending as today. After rename, never claim pending exists: fail-closed quarantine or mark the actual output with a bounded failure classification, report its real location, and ensure downstream rejects it. Add a synthetic final-parent-fsync failure test asserting no valid-looking final output and truthful retained evidence.

findings.title: The no-worktree-source-read claim does not reject a receipt or afterimage located inside a worktree
findings.proof: protected_roots uses repository/common/worktree/receipt roots only to reject the output destination. load_overlays accepts the receipt parent and reads receipt-parent/afterimages without checking the receipt or resolved afterimage files are outside repository and listed-worktree roots.
findings.impact: A hash-valid source freeze placed under a dirty worktree is accepted while the emitted boundary says worktreeSourceRead=false and the README describes a separately frozen private snapshot.
findings.minimumRepair: Reject the receipt file and each resolved afterimage when that file is equal to or descends from the repository root, Git common directory, or any listed worktree. Do not reject a harmless common ancestor containing separate sibling directories. Add a synthetic in-worktree receipt/afterimage rejection test.

findings.title: Exact raw Git reads do not disable replace objects
findings.proof: Every Git command is invoked without --no-replace-objects or GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS. Git replacement refs can change the object seen by rev-parse, ls-tree or cat-file while the requested object name remains the supplied commit/blob identity.
findings.impact: The claimed exact raw commit view still depends on mutable repository replacement metadata.
findings.minimumRepair: Run all Git commands with --no-replace-objects (or an equivalent enforced environment) and add a synthetic replacement-ref test proving GitView reads the original committed objects.
